projects.title: SEBI-licensed RTA offering end-to-end mutual fund APIs.

caseStudy.subhead: SEBI-licensed RTA offering end-to-end mutual fund APIs.
caseStudy.challenge: Challenge: Win a clear place in a crowded field against BSE, NSE and MFU, and become the first choice for new-age fintechs.
caseStudy.headline: Cybriila

results.value: From about 12 customers in April 2022 to over 160 by April 2026, including BharatPe, Bachatt, Jar and Stable Money. Cybrilla now processes over 6 million transactions a month.

caseStudy.solution: Solution: We couldn’t out-build the giants, so we didn’t try. We picked two things we could do better than anyone and went deep. Fintechs want speed. They want to test an idea in weeks, not months. So the first promise became: distribute mutual funds in 3 weeks. The second: fully managed daily operations, because no fintech wants to run them. Then we made sure the sales team carried that exact message to exactly the right customers.
caseStudy.problem: Grow revenue by bringing on new customers and getting them to increase their monthly transaction volume.

projects.title: A software development agency that later launched its own product.

caseStudy.subhead: A software development agency that later launched its own product.
caseStudy.challenge: Find the positioning and the right customer that would make their strength obvious to prospects, and turn that clarity into closed deals.
caseStudy.headline: MFStack

results.value: With a sharper story, they started winning deals they hadn’t won before, including first-of-their-kind projects like corporate treasury management. One of those builds became the base of MFStack, their own white-label app for mutual fund distributors and RIAs. The positioning didn’t just close deals. It uncovered a product.

caseStudy.solution: Solution: Working closely with their team, I mapped what they were truly better at than their competitors, and what they weren’t. I built the positioning on that honest read, then turned it into a sales story the team could carry into every conversation. We rebuilt the sales script around it and tracked how conversations changed over the following months.
caseStudy.problem: Strong technical work, but deals kept going to competitors and leads came in unevenly. The skill was there. Buyers just couldn’t see it.

projects.title: A digital B2C mutual fund distribution platform with a human in the loop.

caseStudy.subhead: A digital B2C mutual fund distribution platform with a human in the loop.
caseStudy.challenge: The platform was reaching users with little money to spare. About 40% of incoming leads were actually looking for a short-term personal loan, not a place to invest. The task was to find an audience with real savings to put to work.
caseStudy.headline: Perccent

results.value: Registered users grew from around 250 to over 13,000 in 90 days, most of them earning above ₹25 lakh a year. The average investment is up 20x. Early drop-off, once 72%, is now under 20%.

caseStudy.solution: I spent over two months with the founders, digging into the numbers. Each customer cost over ₹2,000 to acquire, and 72% of users left within their first 40 days. The company was burning cash fast. We studied the platform’s strengths, its weak spots and the market to find a position we could defend, and built a pivot plan around it. Two things stood out. Users valued having a real person in their investment journey. And the founders, with 20+ years of experience each, had strong networks of their own. Phase one went after exactly those people.
caseStudy.problem: People signed up. Far fewer invested.

projects.title: A performance data provider for mutual funds.

caseStudy.subhead: A performance data provider for mutual funds.
caseStudy.challenge: Buyers compared FinArk’s features and credibility with established names like Morningstar and Value Research. Businesses started the trial, then never paid.
caseStudy.headline: FinArk

results.value: In the first three months, 1 in 3 trial users became paying customers. FinArk won its first 10 paying customers, and over 60% of them renew.

caseStudy.solution: I was honest about the starting point. A new company can’t match the leaders on features from day one. And with data products there’s little room to stand out on the product itself, because the source, format and presentation are mostly standard. So we took the two positions that were truly ours: better uptime and a clear cost advantage. I reworked the sales script to answer the feature and credibility doubts head-on, and recommended direct channels to build the pipeline: cold calling and partnerships.
caseStudy.problem: Almost no one moved from the free tier to paid.

projects.alt: Person reviewing documents beside a laptop
projects.title: A WealthTech platform for NRIs.

caseStudy.challenge: With hundreds of platforms already covering most needs, the task was to read the market and find a position worth owning.
caseStudy.headline: RuDo Wealth

results.value: The founders saw how much money was being left on the table. Of the directions on offer, they chose NRIs. Both live in the UAE, a hub for NRIs investing back into India, and already had their own networks to bring in the first customers. The research turned an open question into a clear market.

caseStudy.solution: I proposed a ground-up study of the market and the competition. It covered where the mutual fund industry was heading, what people were actively searching for, and how competitors positioned themselves. I spent three to four weeks on research and user interviews, then took the findings to the founders.
caseStudy.problem: The founders knew they wanted to build, but not where to start.

projects.title: India’s leading dog behaviour correction and training institute.

caseStudy.subhead: India’s leading dog behaviour correction and training institute.
caseStudy.challenge: K9 School worked with separate vendors for marketing, the landing page, automation and more. No single vendor was the problem. None of them were working toward one business outcome. Everyone was busy finishing their own checklist.
caseStudy.headline: K9 School

results.value: Within three days of fixing the landing page, leads went up 20x. The demand had been there all along. The funnel was blocking it. From there we closed one leak after another, and enquiries and sales returned to a steady flow.

caseStudy.solution: The talent was already there, so I didn’t replace anyone. I took on the job nobody owned: coordination. With the core team, I mapped the full funnel to find where it leaked. The first find was a landing page with a 98% bounce rate. Nearly every rupee spent on ads was sending people to a door that didn’t open. I then had every vendor report their numbers daily, and we tracked each step of the funnel without exception. The leaks showed up quickly, and we fixed them one by one.
caseStudy.problem: Few leads, and most of them weren’t the right fit.
